category_title: Middle school students with diverse learning disorders and low reading engagement
minimal_context: The student is in a sixth-grade class reading a story from the required curriculum.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to read the next story from the required curriculum. Please get your supplies out and begin reading.

STUDENT: (Keeps eyes downcast curtained by hair) I don't have any supplies for the first day of school.

TUTOR: You can borrow this pencil. Please look at the story.

STUDENT: (Looks confused) It's boring. I'm worried that I won't be able to focus on reading a book.

TUTOR: Just try to pay attention and keep reading.

STUDENT: (Puts head on the desk, then leaves their seat for the fourth time in 10 minutes to sharpen the pencil they borrowed, 'accidentally' hitting someone on the way)

options.A: Provide constant 'wake-up' signals to the student during the required reading activity.
options.B: Lower expectations for the student and reduce the reading assignment from three pages to two.
options.C: Pretend not to notice the disruptive behavior, planning to discuss it after the reading finishes.
options.D: Provide diverse genres on a range of relevant topics for the student to choose from.
